title: The suspected pending-prefetch guard did not delay the observed requests
summary: Direct observations found zero returns from the semantic pending/in-flight early-return guard across 975 calls. This particular guard did not explain the two measured slowdowns; native transfer deferrals were separate.
scope: Two active-scoring/prefetch executions at 1,024 and 2,048 GPU blocks, 144 strict request proofs. The smaller case had eight preemptions, four pending binds and three native transfer deferrals.
limitations: No in-flight binding occurred in the new runs, though one existed in historical data. Retrospective bind-to-ready intervals are potential bounds, not measured guard waits. Instrumented timings do not isolate causal throughput loss.
decision: Retain the falsified explanation with its exposure limits. Do not infer scheduler stalls from binding state or treat unobserved cases as measured zeros.
